description: What happens to software after its first release: handling change requests, understanding legacy code, refactoring, measuring debt, mining version history, migrating systems and shipping patches. Students take over a small legacy system in the lab and improve it step by step without breaking it.
modelledOn: Feathers, Working Effectively with Legacy Code
Fowler, Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code
ISO/IEC/IEEE 14764, Software Life Cycle Processes: Maintenance
outcomes: Classify a change request by maintenance type and estimate its impact using dependency and traceability information.
Understand unfamiliar code by tracing it, drawing its structure and writing characterisation tests before changing it.
Apply a catalogue of refactorings to remove code smells while keeping all tests green.
Measure complexity, coupling and churn and use the numbers to prioritise technical debt repayment.
Mine a repository history to find hotspots, change coupling and the commit that introduced a defect.
Plan a migration and a release or patch process with versioning, rollback and communication.

units.title: Software maintenance and change requests
topics: The laws of software evolution and why systems that are used must keep changing
Corrective, adaptive, perfective and preventive maintenance; the maintenance process
Change request lifecycle: logging, triage, prioritisation, approval and closure
Impact analysis: dependency analysis, traceability matrices and ripple effects
Maintenance cost, effort estimation and service-level agreements for support

units.title: Legacy code and program comprehension
topics: Comprehension strategies: top-down, bottom-up and as-needed reading of code
Characterisation tests and capturing existing behaviour before change
Call graphs, dependency graphs and recovering a design with reverse engineering
Breaking dependencies: seams, adapters and extracting interfaces to make code testable
Reading logs, stack traces and debugging a production fault

units.title: Refactoring and code smells
topics: Catalogue of code smells: long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, shotgun surgery
Extract method, extract class, move method and rename as behaviour-preserving steps
Replacing conditionals with polymorphism and introducing parameter objects
The refactoring workflow: tests first, small steps, commit often
Automated refactoring tools and their limits; when not to refactor

units.title: Technical debt and software metrics
topics: The technical debt metaphor: deliberate, accidental, interest and principal
Cyclomatic complexity, lines of code, Halstead measures and the maintainability index
Coupling and cohesion metrics: afferent and efferent coupling, instability, LCOM
Static analysis tools, linters and quality gates in a build
Prioritising debt repayment by cost, risk and business value; recording debt in a backlog

units.title: Mining version history
topics: Inspecting history with git log, blame, diff and bisect
Code churn, hotspots and the link between change frequency and defects
Change coupling: files that change together and hidden dependencies
Finding bug-introducing commits and linking commits to issue trackers
Visualising evolution and simple defect prediction from process metrics

units.title: Migration and modernisation
topics: Modernisation options: retain, rehost, refactor, re-architect, rewrite and replace
The strangler pattern and incremental replacement of a monolith
Database schema evolution and data migration with verification
API versioning and backward compatibility
Case study: moving a bank's batch system to services without downtime

units.title: Release and patch management
topics: Semantic versioning, changelogs and release notes
Branching strategies, hotfixes and back-porting a fix to supported versions
Patch management: vulnerability disclosures, dependency updates and software bills of materials
Continuous delivery safeguards: feature flags, canary releases and rollback plans
Deprecation, long-term support and end of life of software and APIs

units.title: Evolution in practice and capstone
topics: Maintaining open source projects: contributors, issue triage and governance
Maintenance where connectivity and budgets are limited: offline fixes and field updates
Post-incident reviews and learning from failures
Documenting a system for the next maintainer: architecture notes and decision records
Capstone: take over a legacy system, assess it, plan its evolution and deliver the first improvements

schedule.title: Why software changes and the maintenance process
schedule.exercise: Classify twelve change requests for a school fees portal by maintenance type and order them by priority with a sentence of reasoning each.

tasks.title: Sort ten user tickets into corrective, adaptive, perfective and preventive maintenance and assign a severity to each
Draw the change request lifecycle for a mobile money support team as a flowchart with decision points and roles at each step
Plot size and defect data over 12 releases of a given system and test whether it follows continuing change and growing complexity

schedule.title: Impact analysis and the cost of support
schedule.exercise: Use a traceability matrix and a dependency list to find everything affected by changing the tax rate field, then estimate the effort and testing needed.

tasks.title: Mark every module and test case affected by a change to one function in a given dependency diagram
Write a script that builds a dependency graph of a small project and lists everything reachable from a changed file
Estimate yearly support effort for three products from ticket history and compute the staffing level that meets a 4-hour response target

schedule.title: Understanding code you did not write
schedule.exercise: Read a 150-line legacy billing function, draw its call graph, write five characterisation tests, and list the seams where you could safely insert changes.

tasks.title: Draw the call graph and a class diagram for a short unfamiliar program, then mark the three functions that look most central
Write characterisation tests that record the current outputs of an undocumented pricing function on 15 inputs, including odd ones
Break a hard-wired database dependency using an interface, substitute a fake in tests, and show the unchanged behaviour on all prior tests

schedule.title: Refactoring safely
schedule.exercise: Identify five smells in a 200-line order-processing class and apply a named refactoring to each, running the tests after every step.

tasks.title: Label the code smells in a supplied class and name the refactoring that would remove each one
Apply extract method and move method to a long function and show all 12 existing tests still pass after each step
Replace a nested conditional for fee calculation with polymorphic classes, keeping behaviour identical on 25 test cases and measuring complexity before and after

schedule.title: Technical debt and code metrics
schedule.exercise: Compute cyclomatic complexity and coupling for six modules of a given system and name the two with the highest debt interest.

tasks.title: Compute the cyclomatic complexity of five given functions by counting decision points and check with a metric script
Write a script that computes afferent and efferent coupling and instability for modules in a small project and ranks them
Decide whether to repay or defer five debt items in a start-up case, weighing interest cost against a launch deadline, and defend the choice

schedule.title: Quality gates and debt prioritisation
schedule.exercise: Define a quality gate with thresholds for complexity, duplication and coverage, and rank a backlog of ten debt items by risk and business value.

tasks.title: Run a linter on a small project, fix the ten highest-severity warnings and record the count before and after
Add a pre-commit hook in a repository that blocks commits when a complexity limit or test run fails, and demonstrate both outcomes
Score twelve debt items by cost, risk and value, plot them on a priority matrix and propose the order of repayment over three sprints

schedule.title: Reading repository history
schedule.exercise: Use log, blame and diff on a supplied repository to answer who changed the discount function last, how often it changed, and which files change with it.

tasks.title: Use git log and blame in a supplied repository to find who last changed a named line and what the commit message said
Count commits per file over a repository history with shell commands and list the ten most changed files as hotspot candidates
Compute change coupling between all file pairs from commit data and report pairs that change together in over 70 percent of commits

schedule.title: Finding defects in history
schedule.exercise: Use bisect to find the commit that broke a test, link it to its issue, and describe what a churn-based predictor would have flagged.

tasks.title: Run git bisect on a 64-commit history with a failing test and name the first bad commit
Link commit messages to issue numbers by pattern matching and list which issues were fixed by more than two commits
Build a simple model from churn and complexity to rank files by defect risk and check its ranking against known bug-fix commits

schedule.title: Migrating and modernising systems
schedule.exercise: Pick a modernisation option for a monolithic payroll system, draw the strangler stages, and write the data migration checks needed at each stage.

tasks.title: Choose between rehost, refactor and rewrite for three legacy systems in a case file and justify each choice with cost and risk evidence
Draw the three stages of a strangler migration of a clinic booking monolith, marking the routing layer and the retired modules
Migrate a customer table to a new schema with split name fields and reconcile row counts and checksums to prove no data was lost

schedule.title: Versions, branches and hotfixes
schedule.exercise: Assign semantic version numbers to six changes, then plan how a security fix reaches versions 2.3 and 3.1 through a back-port.

tasks.title: Assign the correct major, minor or patch bump to eight described changes and write a one-line changelog entry for each
Create a hotfix branch from a release tag, apply a fix, merge it to main and cherry-pick it to an older release branch
Respond to a published vulnerability in a dependency: assess exposure, choose the patch order across five services and write the advisory

schedule.title: Safe delivery and retiring software
schedule.exercise: Write a rollout plan using a feature flag and a 5 percent canary for a new payment screen, with the rollback trigger and communication steps.

tasks.title: Wrap a new feature in a feature flag and show behaviour switching between old and new code with a configuration change
Roll out a new version to 10 percent of instances behind a load balancer, watch the error rate and roll back when it exceeds a limit
Plan the end of life of an API used by 40 clients: set the notice period, migration help and the criteria for the final shutdown

schedule.title: Sustaining systems over time
schedule.exercise: Write a post-incident review and a short architecture decision record for a failed clinic-record sync that happened over an unreliable mobile network.

tasks.title: Document a small system as a context diagram and a one-page decision record listing three design choices and their reasons
Run a blameless review of a mobile money outage from a timeline of evidence, identifying causes and three preventive actions
Design a patch that a field agent can apply offline from a small signed file, and simulate applying it twice without harm

schedule.title: Capstone: taking over a legacy system
schedule.exercise: Present an assessment of the supplied legacy inventory system with its metrics, hotspots, risks and a three-release evolution roadmap, and show your first merged improvements.

tasks.title: Run the metric script on the legacy inventory system and write down the five worst modules by complexity
Cut the first two improvements on separate branches with tests, merge them with clean history and tag release 1.1
Take over the legacy system as the new maintainer, handling open requests, a security alert and a stakeholder budget cut, scored on the rubric
